title: Hamiltonian Invariance
description: Essential Criteria - The student must correctly state that [H, L_z] = 0 indicates H is invariant under rotation about the z-axis.

title: Optical Theorem Statement
description: Essential Criteria - The student must accurately describe the optical theorem relating total cross section to the imaginary part of the forward scattering amplitude.

title: Born Approximation Explanation
description: Important Criteria - The student should explain why the optical theorem does not hold in the first Born approximation due to the reality of f(theta).

title: Quadrupole Moment Reasoning
description: Important Criteria - The student must provide a valid reasoning that particles with spin less than 1 cannot have an electric quadrupole moment.

title: Phase Shift Sign
description: Important Criteria - The student should justify that the phase shift is positive for scattering from a weak short-range attractive potential.

title: Missing Hamiltonian Details
description: Pitfall Criteria - The student may incorrectly state that H can contain phi explicitly, which is a common misunderstanding.

title: Incorrect Optical Theorem
description: Pitfall Criteria - The student might misstate the relationship in the optical theorem or omit the imaginary part of f(0).

title: Quadrupole Moment Misconception
description: Pitfall Criteria - The student may incorrectly claim that the proton can have an electric quadrupole moment without proper justification.
